title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a preliminary section (§1.1) of notes on Gauss-Manin connections and Picard-Fuchs equations. The aim is to set up a dictionary of equivalent incarnations of a 'PGL_2-torsor' over a scheme X. The next pages (1.7, 1.8) refine this to P^1-bundles with a section and then add connections, i.e. second-order (Picard-Fuchs / uniformization type) equations.

The page lists the following equivalent data over X:
(a) A P^1-bundle f: P -> X, i.e. a Brauer-Severi scheme of relative dimension 1.
(b) Locally free rank-2 modules E 'modulo twisting by invertible modules'. This is only meaningful locally or as a gerbe-like datum, which is why he adds that L is defined only locally on X and up to f^*(line bundle).
(c) Azumaya algebras M of rank 4.
(d) Lie algebra forms g of pgl_2. Grothendieck writes pgl(1), indexing by the projective dimension.
(d') Forms g' of sl_2.
(e) Group forms G of PGL_2.
(e') Group forms G' of SL_2.
A marginal bracket ties (d), (d'), (e), (e') to the condition that 2 is invertible.

Constructions from P:
- E = f_*(L), with L of relative degree 1. L exists locally on X and is unique up to f^*(ℒ).
- M = Ě⊗E = End(E) ≅ E⊗E⊗(Λ²E)^{-1}, using Ě ≅ E⊗(Λ²E)^{-1} in rank 2.
- Two filtrations of E⊗E give two extensions:
  - M is an extension of O_X by Γ²E⊗(Λ²E)^{-1}. Here O_X ≅ Λ²E⊗(Λ²E)^{-1} via the trace, and the sub is the trace-zero part (symmetric tensors).
  - M is an extension of Sym²E⊗(Λ²E)^{-1} by O_X, the scalars, which are the antisymmetric tensors.
- Sym²E = f_*(L^2), and T_{P/X} ≅ L^2⊗f^*(Λ²E)^{-1} by the relative Euler sequence. Hence g = M/O_X ≅ f_*(T_{P/X}), and the commutator bracket corresponds to the bracket of vertical vector fields.
- He asks whether M ≅ f_*(P^1_{P/X}(T_{P/X})), with P^1 the first-order principal parts.
- g' = trace-zero elements of M. The map g' -> g is canonical and is an isomorphism if 2 is invertible.
- G = Aut_X(P) ≅ Aut(E)/G_m ≅ Aut(M) ≅ Aut(g) ≅ Aut(g'). He adds the warning 'attention à la car. (notamment car. 2!)'.
- G' = SL(E), the Chevalley simply connected cover. It depends only on P.
- P = P(E) can be recovered as:
  - the scheme of left ideals of M that are locally direct factors of the appropriate rank;
  - the scheme of Borel subalgebras of g (or g');
  - the scheme of Borel subgroups of G (or G').
- Margin: the bracket is made explicit as Sym²E⊗Sym²E -> Sym²E⊗Λ²E (resp. with Γ²). The Killing form is Sym²E⊗Sym²E -> (Λ²E)^{⊗2}, and similarly for Γ².

Check of the queried isomorphism: P^1_{P/X}(L) ≅ f^*E, so P^1(L^n) ≅ f^*E⊗L^{n-1}. Therefore P^1(T_{P/X}) ≅ f^*E⊗L⊗f^*(Λ²E)^{-1}, and f_* of it is E⊗E⊗(Λ²E)^{-1} ≅ M. So the queried isomorphism holds at least as O_X-modules. The more natural algebra description is M ≅ f_*Diff^{≤1}_{P/X}(L,L), whose symbol sequence pushes forward to 0 -> O_X -> M -> g -> 0.

All of this is standard SGA3 / Brauer-group material. It prepares the transition to oper-like data (P with transversal section, filtered g) on the next page.
errors: (b) is not a global equivalence. A P^1-bundle is P(E) only if its Brauer class vanishes, so the 'rank-2 module modulo twists' must be read as a local datum (a gerbe of twisted sheaves). Grothendieck signals this ('L défini loc. sur X'), but the list presents it as on a par with the others.

Aut(g) ≅ G and the equivalence of (d)/(d') with the other data fail in characteristic 2: sl_2 becomes nilpotent and sl_2 -> pgl_2 is no longer an isomorphism. Grothendieck's own warning covers this; the restriction '2 inv.' should apply to the whole of d, d'.
The underbrace formula should read f_*(L^{⊗2})⊗(Λ²E)^{-1} ≅ f_*(L^{⊗2}⊗f^*(Λ²E)^{-1}) = f_*(T_{P/X}). The transcription drops the inverse.
M ≅? f_*(P^1(T_{P/X})) is left open. It is true as modules, but no canonical algebra structure is given; f_*Diff^{≤1}(L) is the natural algebra model.

ideas.what: Equivalence of P^1-bundles, rank-4 Azumaya algebras, forms of PGL_2/SL_2 and their Lie algebras
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1(X, PGL_2) and its incarnations (Brauer-Severi / Azumaya / twisted forms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Le groupe de Brauer I-III), Demazure-Grothendieck SGA3
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (Dix exposés); SGA3 Exp. XXIV

ideas.what: g = M/O_X ≅ f_*(T_{P/X}) with the vector-field bracket; trace-zero g' -> g is an isomorphism iff 2 is invertible
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint bundle of a PGL_2-torsor = pushforward of vertical vector fields
Principal parts / Atiyah algebra description of End(E): End(E) = f_*Diff^{≤1}(L)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Atiyah (1957), principal parts in EGA IV 16

ideas.what: P recovered as the scheme of Borel subalgebras of g / Borel subgroups of G / rank-2 left ideals of M
ideas.modern_name: Scheme of Borel subgroups (flag variety of a reductive group scheme)

ideas.what: Two-step filtrations of End(E) via Sym²/Γ²/Λ² and the Killing form Sym²E⊗Sym²E -> (Λ²E)^{⊗2}
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition gl(E) = O ⊕ sl(E) and its characteristic-free version

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful, characteristic-aware compilation of standard equivalences for PGL_2-torsors, preparing the oper-like data of the following pages. Nothing here goes beyond SGA3 / Brauer-group folklore; the one open question has a routine positive answer as modules.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely '§ schémas' or 'S schémas' rather than '𝔛 schémas'.
'n 2 inv. sur X' → 'si 2 inv. sur X' (bracket covering d, d').
'fibré de Br. Sev. de rang 1' = Brauer-Severi of relative dimension 1.
'f_*(L^{⊗2}⊗Λ²E)' should carry an inverse: f_*(L^{⊗2}⊗(Λ²E)^{-1}), identified with t_{P/X}.
'[ΛB O_X ou car le centre]' → '[NB O_X est le centre]'.
'𝔤' ⊂ M^E' and 'Ě⊗E^L' are probably just M and Ě⊗E with stray marks.
'rev. [univ.] de Chevalley' = universal (simply connected) cover in Chevalley's sense.
